name: Emotional Tone Variance
description: Measures sentence-by-sentence emotional and tonal variation. Human writing exhibits frequent micro-shifts in tone (e.g., from objective to frustrated), whereas AI maintains a rigidly constant, unwavering register.
mechanism: While the 'Emotional Arc' tracks the macro-trajectory of a narrative, 'Emotional Tone Variance' measures the micro-fluctuations of sentiment at the sentence level. Human communication is inherently dynamic; a human writer might state an objective fact, immediately follow it with a frustrated opinion, make a sarcastic quip, and then offer a hopeful resolution. This creates a high variance in emotional tone from one sentence to the next. AI language models, bound by probability and 'helpful/neutral' alignment protocols, suffer from severe tonal inertia. Once an LLM establishes a tone (usually authoritative, informative, or politely enthusiastic), it acts like a synthesizer holding a single chord—every subsequent sentence matches that exact same tonal frequency. This method calculates the sentiment score of every individual sentence and computes the statistical variance and standard deviation across the entire text. A text that 'flatlines' with near-zero tonal variance across dozens of sentences is statistically highly improbable for human psychology and strongly indicates artificial generation.
useCase: Analyzing opinion pieces, reviews, emails, and forum posts where humans typically code-switch and exhibit rapid shifts in emotional register. Detects the 'robotic consistency' of AI.
strengths:
• Excellent for short-to-medium texts where a full 'emotional arc' cannot be plotted, but micro-variance can still be measured.
• Highly effective at detecting AI text that has been prompted to adopt a persona (e.g., 'write this like an angry pirate'), because the AI will maintain the 'angry' tone with unnatural, unbroken consistency.
• Language-agnostic, provided the underlying sentiment analyzer is robust for the target language.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives on naturally monotonic human writing, such as highly technical documentation, legal contracts, or standard operating procedures.
• Extremely short texts (under 3 sentences) cannot yield a statistically significant variance score.
• Does not analyze the meaning of the emotion, only the mathematical fluctuation of its intensity.
parameters:
Analysis: Sentence Tokenization & VADER-style Sentiment Scoring
Metric: Standard Deviation and Variance of Sentence-Level Polarity Scores
Output: 0-100 Tonal Inertia (Robotic Consistency) Score
accuracy: High — 75-85%. A very reliable indicator distinguishing human psychological dynamism from machine algorithmic consistency.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Hutto, C.J. & Gilbert, E. (2014). VADER: A Parsimonious Rule-based Model for Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text. ICWSM.
